title: The 80% Video
article_body:
Ask any experienced salesperson what percentage of the questions they get on sales calls are essentially the same, regardless of who's on the other end. The answer is almost always between 70 and 90%. Prospects ask the same questions about how your process works, what your pricing looks like, how long things take, what the common concerns are, and what differentiates you from competitors. Every single call.

The 80% Video is built on a simple premise: if you already know what those questions are, answer them before the call happens. Put a real person on camera, walk through the most common questions prospects have, and send that video to every prospect before their first meeting with your team.

## What Changes When Prospects Watch First

A prospect who arrives at a sales call having already watched the 80% Video is a fundamentally different kind of conversation partner. They've processed the foundational information. They've already decided whether the basic parameters work for them. The conversation can start at a level of specificity that typically takes multiple calls to reach without the video.

This benefits both sides. The prospect isn't wasting time on questions they'll find answered in the video. The salesperson isn't spending the first third of every call on the same educational overview. Both sides can get to the real conversation faster: is this a fit, and what would it look like to work together?

## How to Build the 80% Video

Start by gathering your sales team for a brainstorm. The goal is a list of the questions that come up on virtually every call. Include the questions about price, process, timeline, common concerns, how you compare to alternatives, and what makes you different. These are your topics.

Then put a subject matter expert or senior salesperson on camera and have them walk through those questions conversationally. The format is simple: address each question directly, honestly, and with the same tone and depth they'd bring to a live conversation. There's no need for elaborate production. A clean background, good audio, and a natural delivery are all you need.

Create a separate 80% Video for each major product or service. The questions a prospect has about one offering are likely different from those they'd have about another. Each video should be specific enough to be genuinely useful rather than a generic company overview.

## How to Deploy It

The 80% Video should live on the relevant product or service page of your website. But the most powerful use is proactive: salespeople send it to prospects as part of their meeting confirmation. A simple note that says "before we talk, here's a video that covers the questions most people have" prepares the prospect and signals that your company values their time.

The 80% Video is one of the highest-leverage tools in the Selling 7. It pays for itself in the first few sales cycles it improves, and its compounding value — better-prepared prospects, shorter cycles, higher close rates — grows over time as more buyers engage with it before they ever speak with your team.

The name comes from the observation that roughly 80% of sales questions are universal — the remaining 20% are where real sales skill is applied.

key_questions.question: How do we know which questions to include?
key_questions.answer: Ask your sales team. Sit in on calls. Review recorded sales conversations. The questions that come up on nearly every call are your 80%. Most sales teams can identify them in a 30-minute brainstorm.

key_questions.question: How long should the 80% Video be?
key_questions.answer: As long as necessary to answer the core questions thoroughly. Most run five to ten minutes. Quality and completeness matter more than keeping it short. A prospect who leaves the video still having major unanswered questions will bring those to the call anyway.

key_questions.question: Should the 80% Video be on our website?
key_questions.answer: Yes, ideally on the relevant product or service page. But the most impactful use is having salespeople send it directly to prospects before scheduled meetings, with a note like 'this video covers the questions most people have before we talk.'

key_questions.question: Do we need a separate 80% Video for each product?
key_questions.answer: Yes, if your products or services are meaningfully different. The questions prospects have about product A are likely different from the questions they have about product B. Each deserves its own video.

key_questions.question: What happens to sales call dynamics when prospects watch the 80% Video first?
key_questions.answer: The call starts at a much higher level. Prospects have already processed the foundational information and often arrive with more specific, focused questions. Close rates tend to improve because buyers are better qualified before the conversation begins.
